points.description: States that the coefficient of excess (excess kurtosis) is a difference/subtraction between two kurtosis coefficients: the kurtosis coefficient of the distribution itself minus another kurtosis coefficient.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only vaguely says it is related to or compared with kurtosis, without stating it is a difference.

points.description: Identifies the reference value subtracted as the kurtosis coefficient of the normal distribution (i.e. kurtosis of the distribution minus that of the normal distribution).
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the normal distribution is mentioned as the comparison but the difference/direction is unclear.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for saying excess kurtosis is the distribution's own kurtosis coefficient minus the kurtosis coefficient of the normal distribution; wording and synonyms are fine. Give 1 mark if only one part is right, e.g. a comparison with kurtosis but no mention of the normal distribution, or the reverse. Give 0 for definitions that only describe kurtosis as peakedness, with no difference and no normal distribution.
